title: The Regenerative Agriculture Assistant
text:
Good agriculture advice has long depended on where you live, what language you speak, and whether you can afford an agronomist. The Regenerative Agriculture Assistant (RAA) opens these knowledges to anyone with a cell phone or computer. You can ask the RAA about planting times, pest problems, seed saving, composting, or what to grow in poor soil. The RAA brings together contemporary agricultural science with ITECK, so traditional practices sit alongside modern techniques.
Open the Agriculture Assistant


Building organic matter, cover cropping, composting, and restoring soil.



Choosing and growing crops as seasons, rainfall, and pests shift.
Threatened plants survive when the people who grow them thrive. Every farmer who can keep a traditional variety healthy and productive is keeping that variety alive. By supporting growers directly, the Regenerative Agriculture Assistant strengthens the communities who hold the world’s plant genetic variety in their fields and gardens.

title: The Regenerative Relations Initiative
text: Indigenous Traditional Ecological and Cultural Knowledge (ITECK) systems have sustained species-rich ecosystems for millennia through intentional stewardship and deep, place-based relationships. Through the Regenerative Relations Initiative (RRI), Copyleft Cultivars offers our community, our collective resources and tools to support the continuance of ITECK systems that communities have stewarded since time immemorial.

title: The Regenerative Relations Initiative
text:
Community Data Governance
A critical element of RRI’s vision and work is uplifting and protecting a community’s right to govern their data.

title: The Regenerative Relations Initiative
text:
Protecting Community Knowledge
We believe it is important for communities to inform and define how their ecological and traditional knowledge is collected, stored, shared, and protected in open-source and copyleft frameworks.

title: The Regenerative Relations Initiative
text:
Community-Defined Protocols & Protections
This work is only possible with relationship building:

Community leadership sets the direction of project engagement, and support is shaped around each territory’s own priorities and protocols.
Reciprocal relationships with land, water, and plant relatives guide our work.
Communities retain full authority over their own knowledge and data.

title: The Regenerative Relations Initiative
text:
Conservation & Land Stewardship
We stand with communities caring for their lands and waters in the face of unregulated extraction and monoculture expansion. The support we will offer to partnering communities in land restoration and conservation will be customized to each community’s ecological context, connecting them with relevant expertise and resources.

title: The Regenerative Relations Initiative
text:
Building Relationships
We are in early relationship-building with communities in Turtle Island and Abya Yala. Our long-term hope is to cultivate a genuine peer network where land-based communities exchange strategies and support directly. This is an early, unrealized idea that we intend to grow toward together. We do not yet have a cohort, fixed timeline, or set schedule of meetings. RRI partnerships are still taking shape, initially as a direct relationship between a community and ours.

title: The Regenerative Relations Initiative
text:
Get in touch
Communities and organizations interested in building a relationship with us can reach the RRI team at copyleftcultivars@gmail.com.

Regenerative Relations Initiative Informational Webinar

Indigenous Knowledge Systems have sustained biodiverse ecosystems for millennia through intentional stewardship and deep place-based ecological relationships. The Regenerative Relations Initiative recognizes that Indigenous leadership in food sovereignty, data sovereignty, and land stewardship offers proven pathways toward ecological resilience and cultural revitalization.


This session introduced the initiative and answered questions from communities interested in the inaugural cohort.


Read the cohort announcement




December 8, 2022 · 10:30 am PST


Free the Seeds


Format: Digital ceremonial release event


Join us for this first-of-its-kind digital ceremonial release event!


We released the long-awaited Freedom Bag Tag, a unique and easy-to-use label you can put on new seed packs to legally copyleft-protect them as a public good and ensure all future users that your seeds have freedom of use.


The Freedom Bag Tag was created over the course of nearly two years, including a very lively public collaboration to create the text of this freedom-assuring Bag Tag. This was the first step in our mission to make copyleft and open-source protections available for the community at large and help us unite together as a community.

title: Copyleft Cultivars
text:
Why this work matters now
Growing seasons, rainfall, and pest pressures are shifting faster than most crops can adapt. The varieties that will carry us through, from drought-hardy landraces to plants that rebuild damaged soils, often live in small farms, home gardens, and traditional food systems. Plant genomics can help us understand and breed for resilience. Those tools should strengthen the people who keep these plants alive, and their future generations should stay in the hands of community.

title: Genomic Galaxy
section: Why are we building a Genomic Galaxy?
text:
Why are we building a Genomic Galaxy?
As growing seasons shift, land stewards and breeders around the world are developing plants that can tolerate heat, drought, flooding, salt, new pests, and rapidly changing ecological factors. Others are breeding plants that help heal damaged land by holding soil, fixing nitrogen, or drawing contaminants out of the ground. These varieties will serve some of the most critical environmental functions for the century to come.
The Genomic Galaxy is being built to keep these plants in relationship with the communities and biomes where their adaptability and resilience will play a critical role in supporting life on our beloved home, Earth.

title: Genomic Galaxy
text:
Join the Genomic Galaxy
We are building the infrastructure, data governance frameworks, and bioinformatics tools to honor those who contribute to the collective knowledge system. We invite you to join us!

Contact us
For general inquiries, email copyleftcultivars@gmail.com.


Be an early contributor
Breeders, seed savers, and restoration practitioners with a new or locally adapted variety can reach out now to be among the first contributors when the Genomic Galaxy opens. Sequence data submitted for Freedom Bag Tag cultivars will help form its foundation. Contact us to get involved.

title: Freedom Bag Tag
text:
Commercial seed packets often come with a “bag tag” that prohibits saving, replanting, or sharing seeds. The Freedom Bag Tag turns that logic around. It is an adhesion contract that takes effect when the packet is opened and is designed to keep the seeds and everything bred from them open to all.


One of Copyleft Cultivars’ primary tools for seed sovereignty is the Freedom Bag Tag. It demonstrates an alternative to restrictive commercial bag tags through an adhesion contract with three binding terms:

No privatization: Third parties’ use of these seeds or their derivatives may not be restricted through patents, plant breeders’ rights, or other intellectual or industrial property rights.
The terms travel with the seed: Any transfer, assignment, or conveyance of the seeds or their derivatives must include these same terms, without exception.
Shared sequencing data: If the resulting material is genetically sequenced, that sequence and relevant supporting data must be submitted to Copyleft Cultivars under a copyleft-type agreement.





“Al abrir este paquete de semillas, usted acepta los presentes términos de afirmación de libertad (“los Términos”). Usted tiene la libertad de utilizar estas semillas de libertad afirmada (“las Semillas”) de cualquier forma que elija. Con el fin de preservar estas libertades, usted se obliga a no restringir, por ningún medio de privatización o de apropiación exclusiva de derechos (incluyendo, sin limitación, patentes, derechos de obtentor vegetal, u otros derechos de propiedad intelectual o industrial), el uso que terceros hagan de estas Semillas o de sus derivados, y a incluir los presentes Términos en toda transferencia, cesión o transmisión de estas Semillas o de sus derivados. Para contribuir a la comunidad, usted se obliga a que, en caso de realizarse la secuenciación genética de la totalidad o de una parte del ADN del material vegetal resultante del cultivo de estas Semillas o de sus derivados, dicha secuencia sea remitida a Copyleft Cultivars (una organización sin fines de lucro constituida y domiciliada en el Estado de Oregón, Estados Unidos de América), junto con los datos complementarios pertinentes y el correspondiente acuerdo de tipo copyleft.”





“By opening this seed package, you accept these freedom affirmation terms (the “Terms”). You are free to use these freedom-affirmed seeds (the “Seeds”) in any way you choose. In order to preserve these freedoms, you agree not to restrict, by any means of privatization or exclusive appropriation of rights (including, without limitation, patents, plant breeders’ rights, or other intellectual or industrial property rights), the use that third parties make of these Seeds or their derivatives, and to include these Terms in any transfer, assignment, or conveyance of these Seeds or their derivatives. To contribute to the community, you agree that, should the whole or any part of the DNA of the plant material resulting from the cultivation of these Seeds or their derivatives be genetically sequenced, that sequence shall be submitted to Copyleft Cultivars (a nonprofit organization incorporated and domiciled in the State of Oregon, United States of America), together with the relevant supporting data and the corresponding copyleft-type agreement.”




The Freedom Bag Tag works primarily as a norm-setting instrument, modeled on early open-source software licenses. It communicates clear expectations and discourages privatization through reputation and transparency, whether or not every clause would hold up in formal litigation in a given jurisdiction. Anyone can use the Freedom Bag Tag on seed packets for newly bred varieties.



We are developing governance protocols for our Genomic Galaxy, where genetic data from Freedom Bag Tag cultivars will be published. We will post further information as this work progresses. In the meantime, here is a snapshot of what to expect when submitting genetic data for a Freedom Bag Tag plant friend.
A dedicated email address for submissions will be posted here. Once it is available, please email the data in a standard format (such as FASTA, FASTQ, VCF, or an SNP genotyping report) along with the cultivar name. Include the testing lab or platform, the date of testing, and where the seed came from, if known. We will reply with the copyleft-type agreement that accompanies your submission.

title: Our Mission
text: Copyleft Cultivars is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit working to protect, publish, and preserve vulnerable plants by stewarding an ethical, open-access intellectual property commons, developing tools for communities to collect and share plant genomics, and supporting local communities to protect and preserve biodiversity.

title: Our Mission
text:
Who we are
Our team includes specialists in bioinformatics, education, data governance, machine learning and language models, community-based participatory research, conservation, ecological restoration, Indigenous Ecological and Cultural Knowledge (ITECK), and intellectual property.

title: Our Mission
text:
The Commons

A community commons for vulnerable plants
Here, “vulnerable” describes wild and cultivated plants whose survival, diversity, or continued care by communities is at risk. These risks can include habitat loss, changing growing conditions, and barriers to saving, sharing, or stewarding seeds and plant knowledge. We use the term broadly, rather than as a formal conservation-status category.
We are building a commons where plants and community knowledges meet to co-create a more resilient future. Whether you come from a background in farming, gardening, academia, conservation, ecological restoration, plant breeding, or land stewardship, you are welcome here.


Soil Health & Remediation
Healthy plants need living soil. Our tools and partnerships share practices and knowledges for rebuilding and restoring degraded ground or eroded land.


Plant Genomics for Ecological Resilience
Because claims of ownership can sever people’s ability to stay in relationship with knowledge and with plant relatives, our open-source tools are designed to strengthen those relationships and keep them intact.
